## Purpose

Test which MetSigDB sets (KEGG, Reactome and WikiPathways pathways, MACdb
disease sets, ClassyFire chemical classes) change as a whole in the contrasts
carried forward: the NRF2 positive control in lung lines and the lineage
contrasts (neuroendocrine vs non-small cell lung lines; colon, kidney and
skin vs all other lines). Set tests can detect weak, coordinated changes that
single-ion tests miss.

**Decision supported:** which sets characterise the contrasts (D34, D36).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`
- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/06_ion_sets.tsv`, `06_sets.tsv` (ions linked to sets, step 06)
- `config.yml`: `enrichment`, `metsigdb`, the contrast definitions

## Methods

Each contrast is fitted as in analyses 05–07 (same lines, design and limma
model). The test is **camera** (`limma::camera`), a competitive test of
whether the ions of a set change more than the other ions, on the
contrast's own linear model. The correlation between the ions of a set is
estimated from the residuals and widens the test's variance
(`inter.gene.cor = NA`); audit/13 showed this correlation to be real.

camera is run in two forms (D36):

- **non-directional** (`directional = FALSE`, main test): do the set's ions
  change more than other ions, in either direction? camera then works on the
  ranks of the absolute statistics (it sets `use.ranks = TRUE` itself). Metabolic sets contain
  substrates and products of the same reactions, which can move in opposite
  directions (e.g. glutamate is consumed when glutathione is made), so a
  coherent change need not shift the set's mean.
- **directional** (default): do the set's ions shift up or down together?

**ULM** (`decoupleR::run_ulm`, a univariate linear model of the moderated
t-statistics of all ions on set membership) gives a set score used only to
rank sets. It assumes independent ions and overstates significance here
(audit/13), so its p-values are not reported.

Ions are linked to sets as in step 06 (D30–D33, D35): an ion belongs to a set
if any of its candidate metabolites does. Sets with at least
`metsigdb.min_ions_per_set` linked ions were tested. P-values were adjusted
(BH) within each contrast, test and resource. For every set the share of
unambiguous ions (one candidate compound) is reported.

**Positive control, fixed before the fit:** the glutathione sets (KEGG
hsa00480, Reactome R-HSA-174403, WikiPathways WP100) change in NRF2-altered
lung lines (analysis/05). The directional expectation (higher) was set
before the non-directional test was added (D36).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/differential.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "08_enrichment")
params <- config$enrichment

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
ion_sets <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "06_ion_sets.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(resource %in% params$resources)
sets <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "06_sets.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Sets tested

```{r sets}
# sets with enough linked ions; index = feature IDs per set
tested <- sets %>% filter(resource %in% params$resources, ions >= config$metsigdb$min_ions_per_set)
count(tested, resource)
set_index <- ion_sets %>%
    semi_join(tested, by = c("resource", "set_source_id")) %>%
    mutate(set = paste(resource, set_source_id, sep = "|")) %>%
    distinct(set, feature_id)
index <- split(set_index$feature_id, set_index$set)
length(index)
```

## 2. Contrasts

```{r contrasts}
# lines and design per contrast, from the same definitions as analyses 05-07
contrast_data <- lapply(names(params$contrasts), function(id) {
    src <- params$contrasts[[id]]
    if (src$source == "differential") {
        spec <- config$differential$contrasts[[id]]
        d <- contrast_lines(data, spec, config)
        terms <- c(spec$blocking, spec$covariates)
    } else if (src$source == "exploratory") {
        spec <- config$exploratory$contrasts[[id]]
        d <- exploratory_lines(data, spec, config)
        terms <- c(spec$blocking, spec$covariates)
    } else {
        d <- tissue_vs_rest_lines(data, src$tissue)
        terms <- character()
    }
    X <- contrast_design(d, terms)
    fit <- fit_contrast(data, d, X)
    list(d = d, X = X, y = fit$y, table = fit$table)
})
names(contrast_data) <- names(params$contrasts)

tibble(contrast = names(contrast_data),
       altered = sapply(contrast_data, function(x) sum(x$d$group)),
       other = sapply(contrast_data, function(x) sum(!x$d$group)),
       ions_adj_p_below_0.05 = sapply(contrast_data, function(x) sum(x$table$adj.P.Val < 0.05)))
```

## 3. Set tests

```{r tests}
run_tests <- function(id) {
    x <- contrast_data[[id]]
    # camera on the contrast's model, correlation estimated per set; non-directional and directional
    camera_run <- function(directional, method) {
        limma::camera(x$y, index = index, design = x$X, contrast = ncol(x$X), inter.gene.cor = NA,
                      directional = directional) %>%
            tibble::rownames_to_column("set") %>%
            transmute(set, method, n_ions = NGenes, direction = if (directional) Direction else NA_character_,
                      score = NA_real_, p_value = PValue)
    }
    # ULM on the moderated t-statistics: score for ranking only
    t_mat <- matrix(x$table$t, dimnames = list(x$table$feature_id, id))
    network <- set_index %>% transmute(source = set, target = feature_id, mor = 1)
    ulm <- decoupleR::run_ulm(t_mat, network, .source = source, .target = target, .mor = mor,
                              minsize = config$metsigdb$min_ions_per_set) %>%
        transmute(set = source, method = "ULM score", score, direction = if_else(score > 0, "Up", "Down"),
                  p_value = NA_real_) %>%
        left_join(lengths(index) %>% tibble::enframe("set", "n_ions"), by = "set")
    bind_rows(camera_run(FALSE, "camera, any direction"), camera_run(TRUE, "camera, directional"), ulm) %>%
        mutate(contrast = id)
}
results <- bind_rows(lapply(names(contrast_data), run_tests)) %>%
    separate(set, into = c("resource", "set_source_id"), sep = "\\|", remove = FALSE) %>%
    group_by(contrast, method, resource) %>%
    mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p_value, "BH")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    left_join(select(sets, resource, set_source_id, set_label, unambiguous_ions, share_unambiguous),
              by = c("resource", "set_source_id"))
readr::write_tsv(results, file.path(output_dir, "enrichment_results.tsv"))

results %>%
    filter(method != "ULM score") %>%
    group_by(contrast, resource, method) %>%
    summarise(tested = n(), fdr_below_0.05 = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = fdr_below_0.05) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Sets with FDR < 0.05 per contrast, resource and test")
```

## 4. Positive control

```{r positive-control}
pc <- params$positive_control
results %>%
    filter(contrast == pc$contrast) %>%
    # rank among the tested sets of the resource: by p-value for camera, by score for ULM
    group_by(method, resource) %>%
    mutate(rank = if_else(method == "ULM score", rank(-score), rank(p_value)), sets = n()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(set_source_id %in% pc$sets) %>%
    transmute(method, resource, set_source_id, set_label, n_ions, share_unambiguous, direction,
              score = round(score, 2), p_value = signif(p_value, 2), fdr = signif(fdr, 2),
              rank = paste(rank, "of", sets)) %>%
    arrange(set_source_id, method)
```

## 5. camera and the ULM ranking

```{r agreement, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
# directional camera (signed -log10 p) against the ULM score, per set and contrast
signed <- results %>%
    filter(method %in% c("camera, directional", "ULM score")) %>%
    mutate(value = if_else(method == "ULM score", score, -log10(p_value) * if_else(direction == "Up", 1, -1))) %>%
    select(contrast, set, method, value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = value) %>%
    filter(!is.na(`camera, directional`), !is.na(`ULM score`))
signed %>% group_by(contrast) %>%
    summarise(sets = n(), spearman = round(cor(`camera, directional`, `ULM score`, method = "spearman"), 2),
              .groups = "drop")

p <- ggplot(signed, aes(`camera, directional`, `ULM score`)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~contrast) +
    labs(x = "camera directional, signed -log10 p", y = "ULM score", title = "camera vs ULM ranking") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "methods", output_dir, width = 8, height = 6)
p
```

## 6. Correlation between ions

camera estimates the correlation of the ions within each set. For comparison,
the same is computed for all ion pairs from the residuals of each contrast's
model. If ions are correlated throughout the data, a set is not more coherent
than a random group of ions, and a test assuming independent ions (ULM) is
too optimistic. For reference, limma's default for camera is a preset
correlation of 0.01.

```{r correlation}
bind_rows(lapply(names(contrast_data), function(id) {
    x <- contrast_data[[id]]
    within <- limma::camera(x$y, index = index, design = x$X, contrast = ncol(x$X), inter.gene.cor = NA)$Correlation
    residual <- residuals(limma::lmFit(x$y, x$X), x$y)
    all_pairs <- cor(t(residual))
    preset <- limma::camera(x$y, index = index, design = x$X, contrast = ncol(x$X))
    tibble(contrast = id,
           within_set_correlation = round(median(within), 3),
           all_ion_pairs_abs_correlation = round(median(abs(all_pairs[upper.tri(all_pairs)])), 3),
           expected_abs_if_independent = round(sqrt(2 / (pi * (ncol(x$y) - ncol(x$X)))), 3),
           camera_preset_0.01_fdr_below_0.05 = sum(preset$FDR < 0.05))
}))
```

## 7. Top sets per contrast

Sets with FDR < 0.05 in the non-directional camera test, with the
directional result and the ULM score:

```{r top}
wide <- results %>%
    select(contrast, set, resource, set_source_id, set_label, n_ions, share_unambiguous, method, direction, fdr, score) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = c(direction, fdr, score)) %>%
    transmute(contrast, resource, set_source_id, set_label, n_ions, share_unambiguous,
              fdr_any = signif(`fdr_camera, any direction`, 2),
              fdr_directional = signif(`fdr_camera, directional`, 2),
              direction = `direction_camera, directional`,
              ulm_score = round(`score_ULM score`, 2))
hits <- wide %>% filter(fdr_any < 0.05) %>%
    arrange(contrast, factor(resource, levels = params$resources), fdr_any)
hits %>% count(contrast, resource) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = resource, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
preview_table(hits, caption = "Sets with FDR < 0.05 (camera, any direction)")
readr::write_tsv(wide, file.path(output_dir, "enrichment_summary.tsv"))
```

```{r top-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 9}
# up to eight sets per contrast, pathway resources first
top <- hits %>%
    group_by(contrast) %>%
    arrange(factor(resource, levels = params$resources), fdr_any, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = 8) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(label = paste0(substr(set_label, 1, 45), " (", resource, ")"))
# skipped when no set is significant
if (nrow(top) > 0) {
p <- ggplot(top, aes(-log10(fdr_any), reorder(label, -log10(fdr_any)), fill = share_unambiguous)) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(~contrast, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey80", high = "#0072B2", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "camera (any direction), -log10 FDR", y = NULL, fill = "Share of\nunambiguous ions",
         title = "Sets changing in each contrast") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "top_sets", output_dir, width = 10, height = 9)
p
}
```

## Interpretation

- **No set reaches FDR < 0.05 in any contrast**, neither non-directionally
  nor directionally. The smallest FDR is 0.087 (non-directional,
  neuroendocrine vs non-small cell lung lines). With the correlation between
  ions accounted for (audit/13), 20–40 linked ions per set and up to 638 sets
  per resource, set-level effects of this size do not survive the multiple
  testing.
- **The positive control ranks near the top but is not significant after
  correction.**
  - WikiPathways Glutathione metabolism (WP100, now reached through the
    cross-reference, D35) is 4th of 139 WikiPathways sets in the
    non-directional test (p = 0.043) and 2nd by ULM score.
  - Reactome Glutathione synthesis and recycling is 14th of 638 (p = 0.073).
  - KEGG Glutathione metabolism is lower (43rd of 86, p = 0.34). Of its 24
    linked ions, only the five glutathione-related ions and glutamate change
    (step 06, audit/13).
  - The non-directional test ranks the glutathione sets higher than the
    directional one, as expected when products rise and a substrate falls.
- **camera and the ULM score rank the sets alike** (Spearman 0.87–0.98 per
  contrast), so the ranking is robust to the method; only its significance
  depends on how the correlation is handled.

**Conclusion:** at the set level these data support rankings, not
significance claims. The enrichment is reported as the camera ranking
(non-directional and directional p-values, FDR) with the ULM score, and the
positive control is described as "near the top" rather than as passed. The
ion-level positive control (analysis/05) remains the evidence that the
NRF2–glutathione relationship is captured.
